text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that context. On a scale of 0 to 10, how would you rate your current pain level, and does the finger feel stiff or difficult to bend? I also need to know if you have noticed any numbness, tingling, or if the finger appears crooked or deformed compared to the left hand.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your symptoms, specifically the inability to flex the distal joint after a forceful pull, this sounds like a tendon injury. Can you confirm if there is any tenderness directly at the tip of the finger, and have you tried to make a fist recently to see if the finger stays straight while the others curl?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The X-ray rules out fracture, so this points strongly to a tendon injury. Can you confirm if you can actively flex the distal joint at all, or is it completely stuck in extension? I also need to know if you have any numbness or tingling in the fingertip to rule out nerve involvement.

REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_Right_Hand_Soft_Tissue

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal ultrasound is unexpected given the classic mechanism and physical exam findings, which strongly point to a rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon, commonly known as Jersey Finger. The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint after a forceful pull, combined with the resting extension and negative X-ray, is diagnostic despite the imaging result.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Rupture)
